newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Notionnel vols shrug off finance audit.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Notionnel vols shrug off finance audit.

text.p: Implied volatility of French debt options traded on the MATIF was unchanged to slightly better bid on Monday after a finance audit in France failed to inspire the market, traders said.

The audit, called for by the new Socialist-led government, showed that the 1997 public deficit was running at 3.5-3.7 percent of gross domestic product, well above the Maastricht Treaty's three percent reference level.
"There was nothing surprising as the overshoot was already in the market," said Jonathan Morris, options broker at Finacor in Paris. "Volatility fell on Friday, and is better bid now."
August serial options' volatility was trading at 4.25 percent, up from 4.15 percent on Friday. September was unchanged at 4.40 percent mid.
By 1310 GMT, September notionnel futures were down 0.14 at 130.22.
French budget minister Christian Sautter said the government was facing a budget deficit of 312-322 billion francs, 27-37 billion frans higher than budgeted.

Finance minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said France would meet the Maastricht treaty criteria to qualify for a single European currency in the same conditions as its European Union partners. He announced a series of budget measures to cut 32 billion francs from the deficit in 1997.

"Everyone knows the EMU picture for France is not brilliant," said a trader at a French house. "But until there is a more concrete idea that France will actually fail to be part of the euro, vol is pretty stuck."
However, he said there was some talk that a technical decline could move vol, particularly if the futures fell through support around the 130.00/129.90 level.

The major trade in September options was buying of ratio call spreads, at the 128.00 and 131.00 strikes. In August investors were trying to buy ratio put spreads, but prices were looking more expensive than on Friday, traders said. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6137
